grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, flour, bicarb, oil, pears, tahini and pumpkin seeds are all plain single foods with nothing factory-assembled.

supermarket.reason: Every item, tahini and pumpkin seeds included, is on everyday Tesco shelves at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a lined tray and a knife, and pressing out and cutting a dough is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: The oats, flour, oil and hot water ratio gives a workable dough, and 5mm squares at 200°C for 18 to 20 minutes will crisp, making 12 topped oatcakes, a sensible snack for four.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers mixing, pressing, cutting, slicing two pears and assembling, and the 20 minute cook matches the bake.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon and cinnamon, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted except water is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Fresh sliced November pears are a main element of the topping rather than a garnish, and a warm-spiced oatcake suits a late autumn afternoon.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholegrain oatcakes with tahini, fruit and seeds make a filling, real-food snack with little sugar.
